brand.title: IQVIA (Production)
brand.subtitle: Knowledge Check — Introduction to CTFS - For TechIQ Attendees

questions.question: How many modules does the CTFS platform contain?
choices: Three modules: GrantPlan, Contracting, and Site Payments
Five modules: GrantPlan, Connect, Contracting, Forecasting, and Site Payments
Four modules: GrantPlan, Contracting, Forecasting, and Participant Payments
Six modules covering budgeting, contracting, payments, and forecasting
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly right—the five modules work together as one unified financial backbone for clinical trial management.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The platform has five distinct modules, not three, four, or six. Review Slide 12 to see each module and its purpose clearly laid out.

questions.question: What is the primary pain point that Rachel, the Site Operations Director, experiences?
choices: Manual financial drag and fragmented visibility across studies and sites
Unpredictable cash flow and time spent chasing multiple sponsors for payment status
Complex regulated technology stacks and integration nightmares
Proofs-of-concept that stall and inability to quantify ROI for leadership
questions.feedback_correct: You've correctly identified Rachel's core frustration—she needs predictability and a single clear view instead of navigating different systems for each sponsor.
questions.feedback_incorrect: That's a pain point for a different persona. Rachel's pain is specifically around unpredictable cash flow and the burden of chasing payment updates across multiple sponsors.

questions.question: Which persona is primarily concerned with modernizing the clinical technology stack without putting compliance at risk?
choices: Gilbert, the Clinical Operations Director
Rachel, the Site Operations Director
Reena, the VP of IT Clinical
Andres, the Digital Transformation Leader
questions.feedback_correct: Perfect—Reena's world is about risk management, compliance, and building a secure, scalable architecture.
questions.feedback_incorrect: That's not the right persona. Reena is the IT leader who needs to trust the technical architecture before trusting the pitch—she's focused on modernization without compliance risk.

questions.question: What is the minimum number of words recommended for the short version of the CTFS pitch?
choices: Under 20 words
Under 35 words
Under 50 words
Under 75 words
questions.feedback_correct: Correct—the short pitch is under 35 words and designed for quick hallway conversations where you have about 30 seconds.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The short version is under 35 words, not 20, 50, or 75. That word count is specifically for hallway-level speed and simplicity.

questions.question: How much money does the instructor notes indicate is lost per day due to fragmented clinical trial financial management in late-stage trials?
choices: Up to $35,000 per day
Up to $50,000 per day
Up to $55,000 per day
Up to $75,000 per day
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly right—$55,000 per day comes from Applied Clinical Trials and is a powerful proof point that makes the cost of inaction very real.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The figure is $55,000 per day, not $35,000, $50,000, or $75,000. This number from Applied Clinical Trials is a key conversation starter in your pitch.

questions.question: What happens automatically when a clinical trial agreement is signed in CTFS Contracting?
choices: The system generates a legal summary for compliance review
Payment milestones in Site Payments are informed and budget alignment in GrantPlan updates to reflect what was agreed
A notification is sent to all sites requesting amendment submissions
The contract is archived and a new draft template is created
questions.feedback_correct: Spot-on—this is the integration story that makes Contracting powerful: signed CTAs automatically trigger downstream systems with no manual rekeying or reconciliation.
questions.feedback_incorrect: When a CTA is signed, two specific automated actions happen: Site Payments gets the milestones and GrantPlan updates to reflect actual agreed terms. That integration is the real differentiator.

questions.question: According to the instructor notes, what is the projected annual savings for high-volume sponsors using CTFS Contracting?
choices: $1 million in annual savings
$2 million in annual savings
$3 million in annual savings
$5 million in annual savings
questions.feedback_correct: Correct—$3 million projected annually for sponsors running 100+ trials per year, assuming two CTAs per site and 200 sites per trial.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The business case figures $3 million in annual savings for high-volume sponsors, not $1, $2, or $5 million. This is based on specific assumptions about trial and site volume.

questions.question: When a buyer says CTFS is new and they're hesitant to commit, what should you emphasize as your primary response?
choices: That Contracting was recently launched and features the latest AI technology
That the rest of the CTFS suite is live and proven with $15 billion in payments processed, and early adopters gain competitive advantage
That the platform will receive free updates for the first two years of use
That a sandbox pilot is the only option for new organizations unfamiliar with CTFS
questions.feedback_correct: Excellent—you're anchoring their hesitation in proven outcomes from the rest of the suite while framing early adoption as a competitive advantage.
questions.feedback_incorrect: When facing the "too new" objection, ground your response in the proven track record of the existing CTFS modules and the strategic value of early adoption, not just technical features.

questions.question: What are the three milestone targets you should aim for in your 30-day follow-up plan after TechIQ?
choices: A scheduled discovery call, a defined CRM opportunity with qualification criteria, or a sandbox pilot invitation accepted
An email exchange, a LinkedIn connection, and a request for budget information
A product demo, a competitive analysis request, and a legal review initiation
A contract proposal, a pilot start date, and a steering committee meeting
questions.feedback_correct: Perfect—these three concrete milestone targets give you a way to track whether your follow-up is actually advancing the opportunity.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The three specific milestone targets are a scheduled call, a formal CRM opportunity, or a pilot invitation. These are measurable markers that show real progress, not just continued interest.

questions.question: Why does the course emphasize never leading with features when competing against point solutions like GreenPhire or Medidata?
choices: Because point solutions are more feature-rich and you will lose any feature-by-feature comparison
Because features change constantly and they become outdated quickly in your talking points
Because CTFS wins on the unification story—point solutions create integration problems on either side, while CTFS solves the whole lifecycle
Because buyers don't care about features and only want to hear about pricing
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly right—you're playing on CTFS's true strength: eliminating the data handoff friction that point solutions create, not competing on individual feature counts.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The principle is about playing to CTFS's actual strength—unification across the full financial lifecycle—rather than getting pulled into a feature race where point solutions often look stronger individually.
